seo_title: Cost of Living in Buenos Aires 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Buenos Aires per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: The capital of Argentina with a European character: 90 days visa-free, a café culture and affordable prices in the local currency. The downsides are the long flight, peso inflation and the language barrier.
pros: A European character and café culture
Affordable prices in the local currency
A rich cultural life and tango
Healthcare that's good by regional standards
cons: Inflation and swings in the peso exchange rate
A language barrier — you'll need Spanish

faq.question: Do Russians need a visa for Buenos Aires?
faq.answer: No, up to 90 days visa-free. The period can be extended at the migration office.

faq.question: How much does it cost to live in Buenos Aires?
faq.answer: Affordable with a favourable currency exchange, but prices jump due to inflation. See the calculator above for an exact budget.

faq.question: What language is spoken in Buenos Aires?
faq.answer: Spanish (with a local accent); there's little English, so it's best to learn the language.

faq.question: Can I pay with a Russian card in Buenos Aires?
faq.answer: No, Russian cards don't work. Cash currency and a foreign bank card are more convenient.

faq.question: What is the climate like in Buenos Aires?
faq.answer: Humid subtropical: hot summers (December–February) and mild winters — the seasons mirror those in the north.

faq.question: Why do Russians move here?
faq.answer: Easy visa-free entry, a European atmosphere, culture and relatively affordable living — plus a growing Russian-speaking community.

reviews.text: Buenos Aires is Europe in South America: cafés, parks, culture. The downsides — the long flight and economic ups and downs; getting used to the peso rate takes time.
I fell in love with Palermo and the local rhythm. Visa-free entry and affordable prices are a big plus. It's tricky without Spanish, but people are very open.
